solutionSql: SELECT s.status, CASE WHEN s.weight_kg IS NULL THEN 'unweighed' WHEN s.weight_kg < 1000 THEN 'light' ELSE 'heavy' END AS weight_band, COUNT(*)::integer AS shipments FROM shipments AS s GROUP BY s.status, CASE WHEN s.weight_kg IS NULL THEN 'unweighed' WHEN s.weight_kg < 1000 THEN 'light' ELSE 'heavy' END ORDER BY s.status, weight_band;

rules.howSolved: The CASE tests weight_kg IS NULL first and returns 'unweighed'.
The next branch returns 'light' for weight_kg < 1000; the ELSE branch returns 'heavy' for 1000 and above.

ambiguities: 'heavy otherwise' is read as 1000 kg and above, so exactly 1000 is heavy. Only 'heavy otherwise' states this boundary, and no declared rule covers it.
ORDER BY weight_band uses the database's default text collation. The labels are plain lowercase words, so the order is the same under any common collation.
notes: Read-only item. Each status and band that occurs is returned, so an empty band is not listed. Ran without error on sample, nulls and boundary. Solve time is an estimate.
